sections.h2: Who answers property tax questions in Jacksonville and Duval County?
sections.html:
Two city departments split the work: the Property Appraiser values parcels and decides exemptions, while the Tax Collector bills and collects. Jacksonville and Duval County are consolidated, so both offices post on jacksonville.gov.

The appraiser's Customer Service and Exemptions Division sits at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260, and answers at 904-255-5900. The collector uses the same street, at 231 E. Forsyth Street, with a main line of (904) 255-5700 and a weekday counter that opens at half past eight and closes at half past four. Value petitions go through the Value Adjustment Board at (904) 255-5124.

Branch offices matter if you would rather not drive downtown. The collector lists Yates (main), Mandarin, Neptune Beach, North Main Street, Roosevelt, Soutel, Westside and a newer St Johns Square branch at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121. That branch took over from the former Kernan and Hogan offices, which are permanently closed.

sections.h2: Why does a Duval parcel carry one of six district codes?
sections.html:
The code on a parcel tells you which set of taxing authorities applies, and Duval has six: GS and USD1 for Jacksonville, USD2 for Jacksonville Beach, USD3 for Atlantic Beach, USD4 for Neptune Beach and USD5 for Baldwin.

Each district's total millage is stacked from separate levies. Countywide, the listed authorities are the county itself, the public schools, the Florida Inland Navigation District and the St. Johns River Water Management District. The three beach cities and the Town of Baldwin add municipal levies on top. Inside one district, a business and a homeowner see the same millage unless a statute or local ordinance exempts something.

The appraiser keeps millage charts as PDFs for each year back to 1999, so a seller can compare how a district's total has moved. Public meetings that set the individual levies happen in September, and the dates are printed on the mailed notice.

sections.h2: Which 2026 roll milestones has the Duval appraiser posted?
sections.html:
The appraiser's home page lists the 2026 steps below. Dates for the exemption deadline and the notice mailing are fixed by Florida's yearly calendar, so they repeat from year to year.

Duval County 2026 roll steps as printed by the Property Appraiser
StepDate shownSource
Preliminary tax roll approvedJuly 24, 2026Duval Property Appraiser
TRIM notices mailedFriday, August 14, 2026Duval Property Appraiser
Final tax roll certifiedOctober 13, 2026Duval Property Appraiser
Prior-year roll recertified after the Value Adjustment BoardJune 9, 2026Duval Property Appraiser
Timely homestead filing for the 2027 rollMarch 1, 2027Duval Property Appraiser
Tangible personal property returnApril 1 each yearDuval Property Appraiser

Tax bills from the collector are mailed on or about November 1. If a mortgage servicer escrows your tax, ask which bill it paid before you request a payoff.

sections.h2: How do I file for homestead in Duval County?
sections.html:
Owners who bought and moved in after January 1, 2026 can file online for the 2027 roll, or mail a paper form to Suite 260, fax it to (904) 255-7963 or email it to the customer service address on the appraiser's page.

  • The home must be your permanent residence, or that of someone who depends on you, on the first of January that starts the roll year.
  • Some situations require extra documents mailed in; the online form prompts for them at the end.
  • A previous Florida homestead may qualify you for portability of the Save Our Homes difference.

Filing late is allowed until the 25th day after the August notices go out, which lands in early September. A sold house means the new owner starts fresh: the buyer files for the following roll, and your exemption does not follow the deed.

sections.h2: What can I do if I disagree with a Duval value?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review at the appraiser's office, then file a DR-486 petition with the Value Adjustment Board if the answer does not satisfy you. The petition deadline is printed on the TRIM notice.

Duval changed one practical detail: if your petition asks for the property record card, the card is no longer mailed. It sits online in Property Search under the TRIM record card link, just below the notice section. Call 904-255-5900 if the page will not open or print.

The Board's page warns that petitioners generally have to pay 75 percent of the ad valorem tax, plus every non-ad valorem charge, before the usual April 1 delinquency date, or the petition can be denied. Ask the Board at (904) 255-5124 what your own figure is.

sections.h2: Do the aerial photos on the appraiser's site settle where my lot ends?
sections.html:
No. The appraiser says the imagery does not always show true boundaries and should not be relied on in a purchase. Hire a surveyor and a title company for any sale.

The same page says Florida law requires the office to inspect every property in the county at least once every five years, and that the staff do not enter the interior of homes. Appraisers drive marked vehicles, wear shirts with the city seal and carry City of Jacksonville identification, which is useful to know if someone knocks and claims to represent the office.

The images are also shared with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, Public Works and the Airport Authority, and Realtors and appraisers use them. For a seller, that means a buyer may have studied the roofline before the first showing.

sections.h2: How can Duval owners watch for fake deeds?
sections.html:
The Duval Clerk runs a free Property Fraud Alert. You sign up with a personal or business name, and an alert comes within 48 hours after any document is recorded under that name in Duval County.

The county's pitch is simple: scammers file bogus deeds to pose as owners and then rent or sell homes that are not theirs. An empty or inherited Duval house is an easy target, so a seller holding a vacant property gains the most from enrolling.

Report suspected exemption fraud to the appraiser's hotline at (904) 255-7964. If the name on a family house's deed is that of someone who died, unresolved ownership can affect the homestead; the appraiser's page points to Jacksonville Area Legal Aid and LISC Jacksonville for heirs' property help and notes that probate or another legal process may be needed.

sections.h2: What changes when a Duval home hosts short stays?
sections.html:
Two obligations appear. Short-term transient rentals owe additional sales and use tax to the Tax Collector every month, and furnishings in a rental become taxable tangible personal property.

  • Airbnb, VRBO and similar sites do not send the tax to Duval for users, so the owner remits it. The appraiser's page lists TouristTax@coj.net for questions.
  • Household goods for an owner's own use are excluded, but furniture and appliances in any rental, short or long, count.
  • Anyone owning such property on January 1 files a return by April 1.

Renting the home also ends the homestead, which would raise the taxable value after the next January 1.

sections.h2: What should a Duval seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for a payoff on every open year, confirm the parcel matches the deed, and keep the closing statement. The state deed tax runs seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price, and the recording clerk takes it.

Older owners and veterans may hold separate benefits at the appraiser. A disabled ex-servicemember with 10 percent or more disability gets $5,000 off assessed value, and a deferral under Form DR-570 is filed with the collector by March 31. Ask whether a local older-owner exemption applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Where is the Duval County tax collector's main office?
faqs.a: It is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone (904) 255-5700, open Monday to Friday from half past eight until half past four. A newer branch operates at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121.

faqs.q: When were 2026 TRIM notices mailed in Duval County?
faqs.a: They went out Friday, August 14, 2026, according to the Property Appraiser. The petition deadline for the Value Adjustment Board is printed on each notice, so check your own.

faqs.q: Can I file for homestead online in Duval County?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners who moved into a Duval home after January 1, 2026 can use the online application for the 2027 roll. The timely deadline is March 1, 2027, and late filing runs to early September.

faqs.q: Does Airbnb collect Duval tourist tax for me?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser's page states that hosting sites do not remit tax directly to Duval County for any users, so the property owner must remit it to the Tax Collector's office.

faqs.q: How do I get notified if someone records a deed under my name?
faqs.a: Sign up for the Duval Clerk's free Property Fraud Alert at duvalclerk.gov. It watches a personal or business name and emails you within 48 hours of a matching recording.
